name: White-pottery jar placed in Shang tomb M331
summary: A broken white pottery jar and lid were placed in late Shang tomb M331 at Xiaotun, Anyang, an example of fine white ware used as grave goods.
description: The fragmented white pottery jar and lid R000167 placed in Hsiao-t’un tomb M331, Anyang.
tier_reason: Prefer fine detail for the particular burial jar; the custodian verifies the object, not its equivalence in consequence to a general material process. This is a scoped consequence judgement, not a reward for documentation or representation.

impact.note: One grave vessel witnessing an existing fine ware, with nothing later resting on it.

date.label: by c. 1050 BCE (contextual)
date.basis: M331 is a Shang/Yinxu tomb, with contested more precise dating; c. 1050 BCE is a rounded broad end of the Yinxu context, not a directly measured deposition date.

events.statement: A broken white pottery jar and lid were placed in the Shang burial at Hsiao-t’un tomb M331.
applications: placement of pottery in a burial
events.population: People who placed grave goods in Hsiao-t’un tomb M331
events.caveats: The institute interprets the jar as broken before burial; the reason for breakage and any prior use are unknown. M331 dating is contested, so the mid-eleventh-century BCE terminus is a broad approximate Yinxu context, not a measured deposition date. No stoneware firing temperature is asserted for this jar.
